raw_response:
My reasoning:

I've been farming this same 7.5 mu for 35 years, so I know what works here. My main system is cabbage-chili on the biggest piece — about 5 mu. Cabbage goes in spring, then chili after. I keep about 1 mu for maize because we need some grain, and small patches of eggplant and kidneybean — half a mu each — for the family and to sell a bit at the market. That adds up to 7.5 mu.

For seeds, I buy hybrid cabbage and chili from the county seed shop — the neighbors all switched years ago and the heads are bigger, the chili more uniform. For maize I use hybrid too, everyone does. Eggplant I plant a local improved variety. Kidneybean I save seed from last year, that's the traditional way and it still works fine.

Fertilizer is my biggest expense. For cabbage I put two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, about 50 kg per mu, then topdress urea twice — maybe 30 kg total. That comes out around 22 kg N, 8 kg P, 8 kg K per mu, plus I add potassium sulfate at heading because neighbors say it makes the heads firmer. Chili needs more potassium so I add extra. Maize I give less — one bag of compound plus some urea at the big trumpet stage. Eggplant is hungry so I fertilize like cabbage but add more potash. Kidneybean doesn't need much nitrogen since it makes its own, just a little starter.

I'd rather put on a bit extra than see yellow leaves. A bad cabbage head means no money; a few extra yuan of urea is nothing.

Well water is reliable so I irrigate whenever the ground looks dry — cabbage and chili need it often, maize only during drought. Pests are worst on chili and eggplant, I spray whenever I see holes in leaves or whiteflies. Cabbage caterpillars too.

I plough before cabbage planting to turn in stalks, rotary till for the quick turnarounds.
